units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay, I'm out. I need to sit down.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: You did well. Welcome to Museumplein.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Museum square.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A big open lawn, with the Rijksmuseum at one end, the Van Gogh Museum along one side, and the Concertgebouw at the top.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: What's the red brick one?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: That's the Concertgebouw, the concert hall.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It opened in 1888, just three years after the Rijksmuseum.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Its orchestra is among the best known in the world, and the acoustics are famous.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: A neat little quarter.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A deliberate one. This was open ground at the edge of the city in the nineteenth century.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: In 1883 it was a world fair site, and then it was turned into this cultural district, so the museums stand together.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Not a stage for tourists.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Though that has happened. You may have seen photos of a giant sign here spelling out "I amsterdam".

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: I have.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It stood on this lawn for years, a favorite for pictures.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It was removed in 2018, and the city decided that it brought too many crowds.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So if you came for the photo.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Sorry, no photo. But look around.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: There's a pond in winter that becomes an ice rink, and a lawn where people lie down and eat sandwiches.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And the Van Gogh Museum?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It opened in 1973. It holds the largest collection of Van Gogh's work anywhere, thanks to his family, who kept the paintings and later gave them to the nation.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: His brother.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: His brother Theo, who supported him, and then Theo's family.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's a moving place, and it needs a ticket booked long in advance, so we're not planning it today, but look at the building as you pass.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay, I need a coffee.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Or champagne.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Wait. Is that allowed?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: You told us in the request that you care about champagne.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: I did. Because I'm a person with priorities.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Right. So here's the plan. In De Pijp, the neighborhood just east of here, there are plenty of cafes with small glasses and nice terraces.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: You've got about two hours before the brewery.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Sit somewhere, order a glass, and watch the bicycles go by.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And we continue.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: We continue. Walk east along the canal side, toward the Albert Cuyp market.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: How far?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Ten minutes. Pause now if you'd like to sit on the grass.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Pausing. Don't talk.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: I wouldn't dream of it.
